page: Microsoft Azure D2as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor managed by Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provisions 2 dedicated vCPUs executed across a single physical core with 2 threads per core, operating at a 3.7 GHz clock speed. Memory is allocated at 8.0 GB, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Supported CPU capabilities include AVX-512 extensions (f, vnni, bf16) as well as AES and SHA-NI cryptographic instructions. This instance type includes no local storage and does not feature GPU hardware, necessitating external network-attached volumes for persistent data storage.

Benchmark evaluation shows a distinct divergence between single-threaded efficiency and aggregate multi-core throughput. The 3.7 GHz AMD processor yields strong single-core results, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core (3,078.88) and Geekbench single-core (1,952.0). Conversely, aggregate capacity is limited by the single physical core configuration, resulting in bottom-quartile scores across stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core (2,413.0), and PassMark CPU tests (3,834.04). Memory bandwidth registers as weak to poor for read workloads, while large-block uncached writes sit in the middle 50% at 27.73 GB/sec.

The combination of moderate RAM, fast single-core clocking, and limited core density makes the D2as_v6 cost efficient for low-complexity environments. It performs poorly under concurrent database stress and records low throughput for static web delivery (3.44 GB/sec) and Redis sets. Consequently, the instance is appropriate for microservices, lightweight web servers, task automation workers, and staging environments that benefit from strong single-core performance without demanding high thread counts or local disk IOPS.
description: Microsoft Azure D2as_v6 is an entry-level general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor at 3.7 GHz under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core, 8.0 GB of system memory, and no bundled local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark profiles highlight strong single-core performance in the top 25% of evaluated systems, offset by bottom-quartile multi-core and database transaction throughput due to the dual-thread ceiling. Memory reads fall into the lower quartiles, while uncached write bandwidth achieves median levels. The hardware configuration provides a cost-effective operational profile for lightweight web serving, small microservices, asynchronous task processing, and development workloads with modest resource requirements.
